overview.summary: Boehringer Ingelheim is a privately held pharma company with historic strength in respiratory (Spiriva franchise), cardiometabolic (Jardiance with Lilly), and animal health. Their immunology/derm pivot centers on spesolimab (Spevigo), the first approved biologic for generalized pustular psoriasis (GPP), representing a niche but meaningful derm entry. The company is building out inflammation/immunology as a growth pillar alongside oncology expansion.
keyStrengths: Spesolimab (Spevigo): first-in-class anti-IL-36R for GPP — unique niche dominance
Jardiance ($8B+ with Lilly): largest SGLT2 franchise providing stable cash flow
Private ownership enables long-term R&D investment cycles without quarterly pressure
Strong respiratory heritage (Spiriva) transitioning into immunology/inflammation
overview.threatRationale: Boehringer's spesolimab (Spevigo) in pustular psoriasis is adjacent to Almirall's Ilumetri (plaque psoriasis) space. While GPP is a distinct, rare subtype, Boehringer's IL-36R mechanism and expanding derm presence (BI 764532 in CSU/AD, tozorakimab exploration) signal growing ambition in inflammatory skin diseases. Their private ownership and immunology pipeline expansion make them a rising threat to watch.

financials.guidance: Mid-to-high single-digit net sales growth; continued R&D investment at 23%+ of revenue
